title: lockrot report
description: The document `composer lockrot --format=json` prints, report-2 (lockrot 0.14.0): every flag shown, a verdict scored from them, the score basis, the move, the gate and the baseline as data. Every key is always written and every null has a stated meaning. Objects are open: a field added later validates against this file unchanged; the number in the id changes only when a field is removed or renamed. Closed sets are `enum`s; sets that grow in minor releases (including every set a score-model or fix-model change can touch) are strings with a `pattern` and `x-known-values`, which a strict reader takes as the enum. Every human string is a rendering of fields in the same object or in `run`: such strings carry `x-rendered-from` and are prose, not contract.

generated_at.description: When the run ran: the run clock every years field is measured against.

activity_cache_oldest_at.description: Fetch time of the oldest repository-activity answer served from lockrot's cache; null when every answer was fetched in this run. (report-1)

activity_cache_age_hours.description: Hours from `activity_cache_oldest_at` to `generated_at` on the run clock, rounded to one decimal half away from zero; null exactly when `activity_cache_oldest_at` is null (every answer was fetched in this run, or no activity was asked).

packages_flagged.description: Graded findings: the number at the top of the report.

packages_multi_flag.description: Graded findings with two or more counted flags (the `flags:` line).

not_from_composer_repository.description: How many of the packages checked lockrot asked no repository about: the lock entry carries no Composer notification-url — a path, vcs, artifact or inline package entry, or a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL. Equals the number of findings whose `from_composer_repository` is false.

counts.description: Findings per verdict, all seven required (`.counts.<cause>` is null in report-2: read `.flags.<cause>.leading`).

abandoned.description: `total` = `flags.abandoned.carrying`; `with_replacement` keeps report-1's meaning (the finding's `replacement` names a package), `with_suggestion` counts the rest whose S1 suggests something that names no package.

with_suggestion.description: … whose S1 suggests a replacement that names no package (free text or a URL; `next_step.replacement.package` null).

priorities.description: The deprecated `priority` alias over the four grades + none.

flags.description: Per flag, all seven: an object keyed by flag id at the root.

exposure.description: Direct requirements that pull in attributable flagged packages (see `exposure_rule`), with how many, most first, then by name: the same count S7 carries on the requirement's finding. A direct requirement appears here only when it pulls in such a package; a flagged direct requirement that pulls in none is not listed, and its own verdict is on its finding.

flagged.description: Graded packages the requirement pulls in, as its S7 `data.flagged`.

exposure_rule.description: The rule `exposure` and S7 attribute by: a flagged package that is not a direct requirement counts under each direct requirement it is reachable from when there is at least one and at most `max_fan_in` of them. The direct requirements are this run's: `require-dev` counts when `include_dev` is true. The value is what this run used, not a promise; a minor release may change it. Absent from documents written before 0.13.0.

max_fan_in.description: The most direct requirements a flagged transitive package may be reached from and still be attributed to each of them; above it the package is shared infrastructure and is listed under `unattributed`.

unattributed.description: Graded transitive packages reached from more than `exposure_rule.max_fan_in` direct requirements, vulnerable-only ones included; report-2 adds `lead` and `flag_ids` (the counted flags), and `verdict` is the grade. With S7 they name every graded package a direct requirement reaches.

fan_in.description: How many direct requirements reach it.

libyears.description: How far behind the lock is, in libyears: for each measured finding, the years (365.25 days) between the installed version's release and the package's newest stable release, never below zero, summed. Derived from `findings`: `total` is the sum of the published two-decimal per-finding values, rounded to two decimals (report-1 summed the unrounded values, so its total could differ from the sum of its own rows by up to 0.005 per finding), `direct_requirements` the same over `direct: true`, `measured` the number of findings whose `libyears` is not null, `unmeasured` the null ones by reason, `furthest_behind` the greatest above zero (ties to the first package name; null when nothing was measured or nothing is behind). Every drift counts, healthy patches included: this is not a measure of rot or of security, and not php-libyear's number, which sums composer.json's direct requirements (require and require-dev) and scores an undated package as zero. report-2 adds `packages`.

total.description: Sum over every measured finding, two decimals; null when `measured` is 0, since a run that could measure nothing has no sum — 0 is the answer of a run that measured packages and found none behind.

direct_requirements.description: Sum over the measured findings with `direct: true`, two decimals: the nearest number to php-libyear's. Null on the same terms as `total`.

measured.description: Findings whose `libyears` is not null. `measured` plus every value in `unmeasured` is the number of findings.

unmeasured.description: Findings with `libyears: null`, by the first reason that applies. Every non-null `libyears_unmeasured` on a finding is one of these keys, and each count is the number of findings carrying it. A later minor release may add a key, always written from then on but never added to `required`, since 0.13 documents would then fail. These keys are not a pattern plus x-known-values set: `required` lists the ones this release writes.

branch_snapshot.description: A dev pin (`dev-main`, `2.x-dev`): a commit date, not a release date.

no_stable_release_date.description: No date to trust for one end: no stable release; the newest one undated with nothing dated above the installed version (when something dated is, its date is used and the value is a lower bound); the installed version dated only by a commit its tags share and not by its monorepo parent either (where the parent lists the version, its date is the installed version's); or the lock entry without a `time`.

not_from_composer_repository.description: No metadata was asked for: the lock entry carries no Composer notification-url — a path, vcs, artifact or inline package entry, or a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL.

metadata_unavailable.description: Metadata was asked for and did not come: not listed, offline, budget, transport.

furthest_behind.description: The measured finding furthest behind, ties to the first package name; null when nothing was measured or nothing measured is behind.

packages.description: The number of findings in the document (`packages_checked`): `measured` plus the `unmeasured` counts.

baseline.description: How the run compared with the baseline file: non-null whenever the run read one (report-1's rule), its counts from the findings' `baseline.status` (zeros allowed: a run whose remaining findings all score 0 still names the file and its stale entries); null when no baseline file was read.

data_date.description: The oldest non-null finding `data_date`, a datetime as on the finding; null when no finding read repository data (a lock with no finding, or one whose packages all came from vcs or path).

notes.description: The run notes' text, one per `note_details` entry at the same index.

items.description: Prose, not contract; key on the fields it is rendered from.

note_details.description: The run notes, typed (report-1, with six more codes).

findings.description: One per analysed package, in `rank` order.

allOf.description: `activity_cache_age_hours` is null exactly when `activity_cache_oldest_at` is.
A finding stands against a baseline only when the run read one: the root `baseline` is null only when every finding's `baseline` is null.
The root's `include_dev` (report-1) equals `run.include_dev`.
The run fails exactly when something tripped it: `gate.fails` ⇔ `gate.tripped_by` is not empty.
A `check` run applies fail-on and a `generate_baseline` run does not (`gate.fail_on_applied`); a mode this schema does not list is not constrained.
Where fail-on is not applied no finding fails.
Where fail-on is applied a finding that reaches it fails unless something exempts it.
`fail_on` is among `gate.tripped_by` exactly when some finding fails, and `gate.failing` is 0 exactly when none does.

envelope.description: Who wrote the document and under which schema number.

version.description: The lockrot release that wrote the document.

schema.description: The document schema number this file describes: 2 (report-1 documents name report-1.json).

dateTime.description: An ISO 8601 date-time with its offset, as lockrot writes every instant (`2026-10-01T17:39:31+00:00`).

level.description: A signal's own level, as report-1 (`info`, `warn`, `high`); kept for consumers, never printed beside a grade. Closed.

years.description: Years elapsed, counted up to `generated_at`, one decimal, written as PHP json_encode writes a float under serialize_precision=-1, so a whole value is an integer (`4`, never `4.0`); print it with one decimal. The one-decimal rule is stated, not encoded: `multipleOf: 0.1` has no exact binary form and standard validators (ajv, python-jsonschema) reject a third of all tenths with it; only `multipleOf: 0.5` is used, which is exact.

datedBy.description: The monorepo the dates were read from through its `replace` list (a package split out of laravel/framework or symfony/symfony), null when they are the package's own.

forgeId.description: The kind of repository host a note is about: `github`, `gitlab` (gitlab.com and every host in Composer's `gitlab-domains`) or `bitbucket`. An open set: a later release can add a host; read one you do not know as "other". The display name (`GitHub`) is the explanation's `activity.forge`, which is not this set.

metadataFailureReason.description: Why metadata did not come: `offline` (`--offline`, and Composer's cache had no copy), `install_time_budget` (the install-time budget ran out before the package was asked for), `no_versions` (the repository lists the package, and no version it serves is left), `fetch_failed` (any failure not given a more specific reason: a transport error, or what a repository threw, also under `--offline`; a later minor release may move cases out of it into new reasons). `message` carries the words. An open set: read a reason you do not know as another failure.

repositoryActivityNotCheckedReason.description: Why no repository host was asked about activity at all: `install_time_budget` (the metadata pass used the whole install-time budget). An open set: read a reason you do not know as another reason.

forgeRepository.description: One repository on a repository host, with the keys S3 and S4 use: `host` as Composer names it (`github.com`, `gitlab.example.org`, possibly with a port or a path prefix) and `repo`, the path there (`owner/repo`, or `group/sub/project` on GitLab).

host.description: The host as Composer names it (`github.com`, possibly with a port or a path prefix).

repo.description: The path on the host (`owner/repo`, or `group/sub/project` on GitLab).

failedForgeRepository.description: One repository on a repository host that got no answer, with what the host said or the transport error, as `forgeRepository` plus `message`.

host.description: The host as Composer names it.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

originKind.description: What lockrot could tell about where the lock entry came from. `packagist`: its notification-url reports to packagist.org (packagist.org, or a mirror that keeps packagist.org's notify URL). `composer`: its notification-url reports to any other host (Private Packagist, WP Packages, Drupal, a Satis with a notify URL, a registry lockrot does not know, or a definition that declares one itself). These two are exactly the kinds whose `from_composer_repository` is true. `path`: its dist is a local directory (a `path` repository). `vcs`: its source is a VCS repository the manifest lists. `artifact`: its dist is an archive inside an `artifact` repository the manifest lists. `package`: an inline `package` definition in the manifest gives exactly this entry. `unknown`: none of these could be decided: a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL (asset-packagist.org, a Satis without one, some packagist mirrors), a repository listed before the one that matches that could have served the name, a VCS repository renamed or removed since, or a run without composer.json. lockrot's kinds are lower-case words; `<vendor>:<name>` is reserved for a kind that does not come from lockrot. A kind keeps its meaning and its `from_composer_repository` value. An open set: a later minor release can add a kind, which may take entries out of `unknown`; read one you do not know by `from_composer_repository`, show it as written, and link nothing. The order of `x-known-values` is not the order lockrot decides in.

originRegistry.description: The Composer repository the entry came from, named by the host its notification-url reports to, when lockrot knows it: `packagist.org`, `repo.packagist.com` (Private Packagist; the organisation is never written), `wp-packages.org` or `packages.drupal.org`. `packagist.org` exactly when `kind` is `packagist`. Null for every other kind, and for a Composer repository lockrot does not know, whose host is not written: a private registry's host stays out of a published report. A label, never a template: build no URL from it. An open set: a later minor release can name another registry.

signalId.description: A signal identifier: `S` and a number for lockrot's own, as https://lockrot.dev/verdicts/#the-signals lists them, or `<vendor>:<name>` for one that does not come from lockrot. An open set: a later release under this schema number can add an id, so read one you do not know as "other". `x-known-values` lists the ids this release writes; read it as the enum to hold a document to them.

advisoriesNotCheckedReason.description: Why security advisories were not checked: `offline` (`--offline`; advisories are never served from a cache), `composer_too_old` (Composer below 2.4 has no advisory API), `install_time_budget` (the install-time budget ran out). An open set: read a reason you do not know as another reason.

flag.description: A flag id, in the frozen flag order `abandoned silent pinned left-behind old-promise stale vulnerable`. Closed: a new flag is a report-3 event.

maintenanceFlag.description: A maintenance flag id: the flag order without `vulnerable`. The same closed set as `flag`, restricted; the values `lead`, an accepted flag and a baseline entry can name.

verdict.description: The verdict: a grade scored from the counted flags (`critical high medium low`, by `score.total` and the bands of `run.score_model`), or at score 0 the word that says why (`unknown` no metadata, `finished` the allowlist accepted a fired flag, `ok` otherwise). Closed.

grade.description: A grade: the verdict set without its score-0 words, highest first (`run.graded_verdicts`). The same closed set as `verdict`, restricted.

severity.description: An advisory severity bucket in the one order used everywhere: `critical high medium unrated low`; `moderate` reads `medium`, a missing or unknown rating reads `unrated` (which counts as medium). Closed. Compare severities by `run.score_model.severities[].gate_rank`, never by position.

fixKind.description: A fix kind: the class of the easiest release outside an advisory's range, in ease order `update upgrade raise-php unknown blocked none`. `blocked` and `none` double the advisory (`run.score_model.fix_kinds[].doubles`). An open set: a fix-model change may add a kind, which arrives with its row in `run.score_model.fix_kinds[]`; read an unknown kind's `ease` and `doubles` there and show its id.

branchLabel.description: A release branch as lockrot labels it (`2.x`, `0.15.x`, and `0.0.3` for a 0.0.n branch, which is one release wide).

halfPoints.description: A score number in half points: exact, dyadic, `multipleOf: 0.5` (`run.score_model.exact_unit`); a whole value is written as an integer.

advisoryId.description: An advisory's `id` as its Composer repository serves it (Packagist: `PKSA-…`); not promised to be a Packagist id (report-1's S9 rule).

factKind.description: What the fact is: a `flag` (its `id` a flag id) or an `advisory` (its `id` an S9 row id). Closed: the same pair as `without[].remove.kind`; a score has two fact spaces, and a third would be a report-3 event like a new flag.

fact.description: A counted fact a move leaves in place: a flag or an advisory of this finding.

id.description: The flag id (`kind: flag`) or the advisory id (`kind: advisory`); joins `flags[].id` or the S9 row `id`.

clearedFact.description: A fact a move clears: checked for every version the emitted constraint admits, or for the one release `composer update` installs.

id.description: The flag id or the advisory id the move clears.

basis.description: Why it is cleared: `branch_releasing` (left-behind: the branch released within `release-warn-years`), `released_after_ga` (old-promise: the lowest admitted release came out after the target major's GA), `outside_range` (an advisory: no admitted version is inside its range), `tags_only` (pinned: the constraint admits only tags). An open set: read an unknown basis as another reason the fact is cleared.

unverifiedFact.description: A fact lockrot could not check for the move: a counted fact it may not clear (kept as counted), or a flag the move may raise (left-behind on a tag whose line lockrot cannot date); either way `if_applied` is an upper bound (`at_most`).

id.description: The flag id or the advisory id left unverified.

reason.description: Why it could not be checked: `undated` (the lowest admitted release carries no date), `no_release_data` (no release data for the branch). An open set: read an unknown reason as another reason it was not checked.

addedFact.description: A fact the move would raise; every surface names it.

id.description: The flag id the move would raise.

basis.description: Why the move raises it: `released_before_ga` (a tag released before the target major's GA, with an open `require.php`, adds old-promise), `branch_not_releasing` (a tag on a line that has not released in `release-warn-years` while a higher line has, S8's own rule, adds left-behind). An open set: read an unknown basis as another reason.

factBaseline.description: A fact's state against the baseline entry: on each counted maintenance flag's `flags[].baseline` and on each S9 row's `baseline`. Null without a baseline, and always null on the `vulnerable` flag (its advisories carry theirs).

state.description: `known` (the entry lists it), `covered` (a flag below the entry's recorded flag: `covered_by` names it), `new`, `re_rated` (higher by gate rank), `fix_lost` (`update upgrade raise-php unknown` → `blocked none`, compared only at an equal target and fix model). An open set sharing its values with `baseline.worsened_by[].why`. `known` is the baseline's word; `accepted` is the allowlist's only.

since.description: The date the baseline first knew the fact (`known_since`); null for a fact the entry does not know.

covered_by.description: The recorded flag above a `covered` flag ("stale (baseline: below the recorded old-promise)"); null for every other state.

allOf.description: `covered_by` is set exactly on `covered`; a state this schema does not list is not constrained.

holder.description: The holder's own finding in this report, for display only (no score reads it): `{verdict, lead, flag_ids[], replacement, next_step}`. Null for the root, and for a holder that is not a finding of this report.

flag_ids.description: The holder's counted flag ids, in flag order (every list of bare flag ids is `flag_ids`).

replacement.description: The holder's `replacement` (a Composer package name), so an abandoned holder reads "held by abandoned symfony/x (replacement: …)".

next_step.description: The holder's own move; null when the holder's finding has no move (score 0).

oneOf.description: The holder's own move, `{kind, to_branch, constraint}` of its `next_step`, so a sentence writes "its own move, require ^4.4.51" without reading another finding.

heldBy.description: One link that excludes the move or the fix: the root's or a locked package's `require`, `require-dev` or `conflict`.

source.description: Who holds it: `root` (composer.json) or `package` (a locked package). Closed.

package.description: The locked package that holds it; null for `source: root`.

version.description: That package's locked version; null for `source: root`.

link.description: The link that excludes it. Closed.

constraint.description: The constraint as the link writes it, quoted and never interpreted ("requires ^2.0").

allOf.description: `source` root has no `package`, `version` or `holder`; `source` package names the package in `package`.

phpCheck.description: What the release a move names needs from PHP: set on every move that names a branch or a tag (`update require raise-php blocked tag`) and on `security.gets`. A sentence prints its php clause only when `requires` is set; it names the project's lowest PHP from `run.project_php_lowest`.

requires.description: The php constraint the release declares (`>=8.1.0`); null when it declares none.

project_allows.description: Whether the project's `require.php` admits it; null when lockrot could not compare (no `require.php`, or no php on the branch row), never "does not allow".

target_runs.description: Whether the target PHP (`run.target_php`) runs it; null when lockrot could not compare.

raise_to.description: The value to write into `require.php` (`>=8.1`); null when the project floor already admits the release.

raise_size.description: How far the floor moves: closed `major minor patch`; null when no raise is needed.

termMaintenance.description: A maintenance term: one counted maintenance flag. `points` = `weight` ÷ `divisor`; `contribution` is after every modifier.

part.description: The discriminator of `terms[]` (closed): this term counts in the maintenance part.

role.description: The maintenance term's role: `lead` (the first counted maintenance flag, in full) or `corroborating` (every other counted maintenance flag, at its share). Open with `x-known-values`, so a model change cannot force report-3.

weight.description: The flag's points in the model (`run.score_model.flags[].points`).

divisor.description: 1 for the lead, 4 for a corroborating flag in score model 1 (the share `rules[corroborating-share].share`); `divisor` 4 ⇔ corroborating. A JSON integer.

points.description: `weight` ÷ `divisor`, before any halving. A JSON integer: every quarter of a weight is whole.

contribution.description: The term's share of `exact` after every modifier (reach, then dev), in half points; Σ `terms[].contribution` = `exact`.

termSecurity.description: The security term: the deciding advisory, the one with the most points, ties by severity order, then the lowest id. `points` = `weight` × `multiplier`.

part.description: The discriminator of `terms[]` (closed): this term counts in the security part.

flag.description: Always `vulnerable`: the security part has one flag.

role.description: The security term's role: `security` (the deciding advisory). Open with `x-known-values`, so a model change cannot force report-3.

advisory.description: The deciding advisory: joins the S9 row whose `deciding` is true.

severity.description: The deciding advisory's severity, which is not always `security.worst`.

fix_kind.description: The deciding advisory's fix kind (its S9 row's `fix.kind`); `fix` is always the S9 object and `fix_kind` always this string.

multiplier.description: 2 when the fix is `none` or `blocked` (no reachable fix), else 1, in score model 1. A JSON integer.

points.description: `weight` × `multiplier`, before the dev halving (security is never halved for reach).

contribution.description: The term's share of `exact` after the dev modifier, in half points.

term.description: One counted fact's arithmetic, discriminated on `part`: a TypeScript union on `part`, never on position. No key is null-padded.

modifier.description: One halving, in application order: listed whenever its fact holds and a term exists, `before == after` when it removes nothing (then it is left out of `score.text`).

reason.description: The fact that halves: `transitive`, `unreached` (not direct, empty chain), `dev` (packages-dev). An open set.

applies_to.description: What it halves: the `maintenance` part (reach) or the `total` (dev). An open set.

divide_by.description: The divisor (2 in score model 1, `rules[divide-reach|divide-dev].by`); printed by the grammar, never a literal of the grammar.

before.description: The value it halves, in half points.

after.description: The value after it, in half points; the last `after` is `exact`.

allOf.description: A reach halving applies to the maintenance part, a dev halving to the total; a reason this schema does not list is not constrained.

status.description: `counted` ⇔ the part has a term; else why it is 0, by precedence `accepted` (a flag fired and every fired flag is accepted, a lock-only flag on unread metadata included), then `not_judged` (no repository metadata, nothing fired), then `none` (no maintenance flag fired). An open set.

contribution.description: Σ of the part's terms' contributions, in half points.

alone.description: The band the part would reach alone: `alone.total` = ⌊`contribution`⌋.

verdict.description: A grade, or null when the part is 0 (a part has no score-0 word; the page writes "no maintenance flag counts").

allOf.description: `verdict` is null exactly when the part alone is 0.
A part counts exactly when it contributes; a status this schema does not list is not constrained.

partSecurity.description: The security part: the maximum over counted advisories.

status.description: `counted` ⇔ an advisory counts; else why it is 0: `clear` (complete lookup, nothing counted), `unchecked` (`security.status`'s word: the lookup did not complete). An open set.

contribution.description: The security term's contribution, in half points (0 without a term).

alone.description: The band the part would reach alone: `alone.total` = ⌊`contribution`⌋.

verdict.description: A grade, or null when the part is 0 (a part has no score-0 word; the page writes "no advisory counts").

allOf.description: `verdict` is null exactly when the part alone is 0.

of.description: How many advisories count (`advisories_now` sums to it under a baseline).

tied.description: The other advisories with the deciding advisory's points, in the tie order (severity, then the lowest id first).

allOf.description: A part counts exactly when it contributes; a status this schema does not list is not constrained.

band.description: Where `total` sits among the bands: rendered as "critical from 32" and "4 points short of critical".

floor.description: The floor of the verdict's band (`run.score_model.bands[].floor`).

next.description: The next band up; null at critical.

to_next.description: `next`'s floor − `total`, an integer measured from `total`, at least 1; null at critical.

allOf.description: `next` and `to_next` are null together, at the top band.
`floor` and `next` name adjacent bands: 32 at the top, 16 below critical, 8 below high, 1 below medium.

ifCounted.description: An engine rerun with the accepted flag counted, under the allowlist entry's whole accepted set; never computed by a consumer.

total.description: The total the rerun gives; ≥ `score.total` and ≥ 1: a counted flag always scores (report-2 had accepted 0).

verdict.description: The rerun's grade (a counted flag always grades).

role.description: The role the flag would take (an open set, as `terms[].role`).

at_least.description: True only for an accepted `stale` decided without S4 (`degree.liveness_complete` false): a lower bound, printed "at least 8, medium".

modifiers.description: The rerun's own halvings, as `score.modifiers` lists them (reach, then dev; `before == after` when one removes nothing): a score-0 finding has no `score.modifiers`, so a page says "its maintenance counts half" beside the rerun's number from this list.

acceptedFlag.description: A fired maintenance flag the allowlist accepts: listed, weighs 0, reaches no gate, and says what it would add. Who accepted it is `finding.allowlist` (one vocabulary).

withoutRow.description: A counterfactual: an engine rerun on the flags derived again from the signals left once the removed fact's `raised_by` signals go, under the entry's whole accepted set; never subtraction.

kind.description: `flag` (one row per counted flag when the finding has two or more terms; `vulnerable` removes every advisory) or `advisory` (the deciding advisory, whenever two or more count). Closed.

id.description: The flag id or the advisory id removed.

revealed.description: The liveness word the re-derivation brings back once `abandoned` hides it no longer, with its role there.

role.description: Its role in the rerun; `accepted` when the allowlist entry accepts it. An open set.

lead.description: The rerun's lead; null when it has none.

deciding_advisory.description: The rerun's deciding advisory id; null when it has none. Not the S9 row's boolean `deciding`.

at_least.description: True when the rerun is a lower bound: a `without[abandoned]` row read without S4 (liveness incomplete, S2 absent or high), and a `without[pinned]` row on a branch snapshot when a tag could be left behind: the branch table was not read, or S8's rule on some branch row fires or cannot be dated.

allOf.description: A rerun at 0 reads a score-0 word; a rerun at 1 or more reads its grade.
Only a removed flag can reveal a liveness word: a row that removes an advisory reveals none.
`at_least` is true only on a row that removes `abandoned` or `pinned` (the rows whose rerun lockrot could not fully read).
