role.description: The flag's term role, or `accepted`: a label. Whether the flag counts is the join `id` ∈ `score.terms[].flag`, never this word (a later role, counted or not, reads correctly by the join). Open with `x-known-values`, so a model change cannot force report-3.

signal_ids.description: The ids of the signals the flag's sentence reads (`signals[].data`; one source per fact); never empty.

degree.description: Only facts no single signal holds: `abandoned {reasons, liveness_complete}`, `silent`/`stale` `{liveness_complete}`, else null.

summary.description: The flag sentence, `FlagSentence`; never empty. The `vulnerable` sentence also reads `security`, `branch` and the deciding term's `severity` in `score.terms`. Prose, not contract; key on the fields it is rendered from.

anyOf.description: `abandoned`: reasons in its degree, headline `reason` archived or marked.
`silent`, `stale`: liveness degree, headline in years from S2 or S4.
`left-behind`: headline in years of the branch.
`vulnerable`: no degree, its baseline is null (its advisories carry theirs), headline `advisories`; its role is not constrained (open).

allOf.description: A flag names only the signals that raise or date it: abandoned S1 S3 S2 S4, silent and stale S2 S4, pinned S6, left-behind S8, old-promise S5, vulnerable S9; a signal id this schema does not list is not constrained.
`headline.source` is null when `headline.value` is.

checkMissing.description: A check that did not run and raised S10 (S10's `unchecked[]` entry, restated as `checks_missing[]`; `--fail-on=unchecked` reads it).

check.description: S10's check id: `repository_activity` (S3, S4), `release_dates` (the package's age, dated only by a shared commit), `releases` (S9's fix part: releases could not be read). An open set.

reason.description: Why it did not run. An open set: read an unknown reason as another reason.

blocks.description: The signals that could not be read without it.

checkSkipped.description: A check lockrot chose not to run: a decision, not a gap; it raises no S10 and reaches no `unchecked` gate.

check.description: `repository_activity` (blocks S3, S4), `release_metadata` (S2, S8), `advisories` (S9), `release_branch` (S8 on a branch snapshot, which has no release branch). An open set.

reason.description: Why: `unparseable_version` an installed version Composer cannot parse. An open set: read an unknown reason as another reason.

allowlist.description: The allowlist entry that accepts maintenance flags of this package; null when none does. `allowlist_reason` stays as an alias for report-1 readers.

by.description: Who accepted: the built-in finished list, the project's `extra.lockrot.ignore[]`, or an entry lockrot makes for a package type. Closed; the one vocabulary for who accepted a flag.

pattern.description: The entry's package pattern; null exactly on a `type` entry.

version.description: The version the entry is limited to; null when it names none.

reason.description: The reason as written: lockrot's sentence (`reason_by: lockrot`) or the user's words, data never entered into a machine string.

reason_id.description: An id for every lockrot-authored reason (`php-fig-interfaces`, `symfony-polyfills`, `type-metapackage`, …), so a page words it itself; null for a user's reason. Open.

expires.description: The date the entry stops accepting; null when it does not expire.

flag_ids.description: The flags the entry lists (config-2 `ignore[].flags`, echoed under the one name `flag_ids`); null for an entry that accepts every maintenance flag.

allOf.description: Who accepted decides whose words the reason is: a project entry is the user's (no `reason_id`); a built-in or type entry is lockrot's, with a `reason_id`, accepts every maintenance flag, and a type entry matches no name pattern.

metadata.description: How the repository metadata went: `note` stays as its rendering.

status.description: Closed. `read` exactly when `maintenance_judged` is true; a package installed from vcs, path or an archive is `not_from_composer_repository` whatever its verdict, and its `release_metadata` entry (S2, S8 not run) is in `checks_skipped[]`.

reason.description: Why it did not come (`MetadataFailure::REASONS`, the open set of report-1's run notes); null when read.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words, redacted as report-1's notes redact them. Not contract. Null when read.

findingBaseline.description: Where the finding stands against the baseline; null without a baseline file, and null for a score-0 finding the baseline holds no entry for (the writer stores graded findings only). A graded finding with no entry has `status: new`, `recorded: null`.

recorded.description: What the entry holds, as the file stores it; null when the baseline holds no entry for the package (`status: new`).

lead.description: The entry's first flag in flag order (report-1's `previous_verdict`); null when the entry lists no flag (advisories only).

flags.description: The flags the entry lists, keyed by maintenance flag id (an object at the root, in baseline-2 and here); null when the entry lists no flag (an advisory-only entry: an empty map is never written).

known_since.description: The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).
The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).
The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).
The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).
The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).
The date it was first known (baseline-2 stores a date for every fact).

advisory_count.description: The number of advisory ids the entry stores.

first_seen.description: The date the package first entered the baseline, as the file stores it.

target_php.description: The target PHP minor the baseline file was written for (its `target_php`).

fix_model.description: The fix model the entry's fix kinds were classified under (the file's `fix_model`). Fixes are compared (`fix_lost`) only when it and `target_php` equal the run's.

allOf.description: `lead` is null exactly when `flags` is (an advisory-only entry).

advisories_now.description: The counted advisories by their state now, summing to `parts.security.of`.

worsened_by.description: Every fact that makes the finding worse than the entry.

id.description: The flag id or the advisory id.

why.description: Why it worsens the finding. One value per fact, by precedence `new`, then `re_rated`, then `fix_lost`: a re-rated advisory whose fix was also lost reads `re_rated`, and `recorded.fix_kind` beside `now.fix_kind` shows the lost fix. An open set sharing values with `factBaseline.state`.

recorded.description: The advisory as recorded; null for a flag and for a new advisory.

oneOf.description: A fact's severity and fix kind at one time.

now.description: The advisory now; null for a flag.

oneOf.description: A fact's severity and fix kind at one time.

allOf.description: A flag worsens only as `new` and carries no severity; an advisory carries its state now, and what was recorded unless it is new.
A `known` finding has nothing new against its entry: no new, re-rated or fix-lost advisory (each would be a `worsened_by` entry).
`recorded` is null exactly for `new`.
A `known` finding has nothing that worsens it, a `worsened` one names what does.

gateFact.description: A fact whose record is `error` for one gate value.

kind.description: `flag`, `advisory`, or `signal` (an `unchecked` value names each blocked signal once; joins `checks_missing[].blocks[]`). An open set.

id.description: The flag id, the advisory id or the signal id.

findingGate.description: Where the finding stands against the gate values. Text formats render the gate basis line (`GateText`) from `basis`.

reaches_fail_on.description: Whether the finding reaches some value of `run.gates[]`, reading the score and the flags before the baseline (0.13's meaning).

fails.description: Whether it fails the run: it reaches a value, `exempt_by` is null and the root `gate.fail_on_applied` is true; a grade value reads the gate score.

exempt_by.description: What keeps a reaching finding from failing: `baseline` (a `known` finding, or a `worsened` one whose gate score stays below the value). Set only under a baseline entry. An open set.

by.description: One entry per value of `run.gates[]` the finding fails (`by[].value` ∈ `run.gates[]`), naming the facts whose records are `error`.

kind.description: The value's kind, as `run.gates[].kind`. An open set, reason-like (underscores).

facts.description: The facts that trip it; never empty for a failing value.

basis.description: The baseline arithmetic; null without a baseline entry (the gate score is then `score.total`).

verdict.description: The gate score's band; null exactly at gate 0.

limited_by.description: `score` (the full score is lower), `cap` (the new facts bound it; always when `new.total` is 0), `equal`. Closed.

new.description: What the facts the baseline does not cover add, in the score's own term shape; its maintenance terms are a prefix of the score's.

rounded_down.description: `exact` ≠ `total`; GateText renders it as ScoreText does.

terms.description: The uncovered flags and the highest-scoring advisory the baseline does not know.

modifiers.description: The halvings, as on the score.

allOf.description: `new.rounded_down` is true exactly when `new.exact` is not whole.
What `new` adds has a term exactly when its total is not 0.
`verdict` is null exactly at gate score 0.
`limited_by` is `cap` whenever `new.total` is 0.
A failing finding reaches a value and is not exempt; a passing one is exempt only when it reaches a value.

s1.description: S1: marked abandoned by its repository or by the lock.

replacement.description: The replacement as the registry or the lock wrote it: free text, a package name or a URL (data; `next_step.replacement` classifies it). Text, never markup.

replacement_url.description: packagist.org's page for the replacement when it is a package name packagist.org named; else null. Show a link only when it is a string.

s2.description: S2: no release for years (report-1, unchanged).

s3.description: S3: the repository is archived; a degree of `abandoned`.

repo.description: The repository path on the host.

host.description: The host as Composer names it.

forge.description: The forge kind, as the repository reference lockrot asked names it (a self-hosted GitLab is `gitlab`): `github gitlab bitbucket` known; Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub Enterprise are on the roadmap. An open set. Never null: S3 and S4 exist only when lockrot asked a forge.

s4.description: S4: no push (or commit) for years.

repo.description: The repository path on the host.

host.description: The host as Composer names it.

forge.description: The forge kind, as the repository reference lockrot asked names it (a self-hosted GitLab is `gitlab`): `github gitlab bitbucket` known; Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub Enterprise are on the roadmap. An open set. Never null: S3 and S4 exist only when lockrot asked a forge.

s5.description: S5: written for an older PHP major and released before the target's major existed (report-1, unchanged).

target_php.description: The target PHP the release is held against.

target_major.description: The first release of the target's major (`8.0` for `8.4`).

php_constraint.description: The release's php constraint as written.

written_for_php.description: The PHP major of the constraint's lower bound; null when it has none (`*`).

s6.description: S6: pinned to a branch snapshot, or no tagged release.

reason.description: Which of S6's cases fired. An open set (report-1).

has_stable_release.description: Whether the repository lists any tagged version; null when no metadata was loaded.

last_stable_release.description: The newest dated tagged release; null when there is none lockrot trusts.

last_stable_version.description: The version `last_stable_release` dates; null exactly when it is.

tag_relation.description: How the newest tag relates to the snapshot (`older newer same`), open; null when there is no tag or no snapshot time.

allOf.description: `last_stable_version` is null exactly when `last_stable_release` is.

s7.description: S7: a direct requirement pulling in graded transitive packages; context, not a flag. Every graded package that is not direct and is reached from 1 to `exposure_rule.max_fan_in` direct requirements is named by each of them, a package graded by its advisories alone included.

flagged.description: How many graded packages it names.

packages.description: The graded packages it pulls in, in the report's rank order.

chain.description: From this requirement down to the package.

verdict.description: The package's grade (report-1's cause word moved to `lead`).

flag_ids.description: Its counted flag ids, in flag order (never `flags`).

s8.description: S8: the installed release branch stopped while a higher one kept releasing. Every key always written; `branch` equals `finding.branch`.

newest_branch.description: The newest release branch, as lockrot labels it (report-1).

newest_php.description: The newest branch's php requirement; null when it requires none.

newest_within_reach.description: Whether its php admits the project floor and the target.

newest_years.description: Age of `newest_release` on the run clock.

floor_php.description: What holds the newest branch back; null when within reach.

floor_source.description: Which floor `floor_php` is (`project target`), open; null when within reach.

reachable_branch.description: The releasing higher branch within reach; null when none is.

reachable_php.description: Its php requirement; null when there is no reachable branch or its release declares none.

reachable_admits.description: Whether `reachable_php` admits the project floor and the target; null when there is no reachable branch.

reachable_years.description: Age of `reachable_release` on the run clock; null with `reachable_branch`.

suggested_constraint.description: A caret constraint following the reachable branch; null when there is none.

s9fix.description: The advisory's fix: `fix` is always this object, `fix_kind` always the string. Null keys below mean the kind names no fixing release.

to_branch.description: The branch of the fixing release; null for `unknown` and `none` (no fixing release known).

version.description: The lowest fixing release on `to_branch`; null when not known (releases not read). Not the move's `version`.

on_installed_branch.description: Whether the easiest fix is on the installed branch; null for `unknown` and `none`.

php.description: The fixing release's php requirement; null for `unknown` and `none`, or when it declares none.

held_by.description: The links that exclude the fixing release; `upgrade` ⇒ not empty where lockrot read the links.

reason.description: Set for `unknown` (`releases_unknown`, `affected_range_unknown`, `not_from_composer_repository`) and `none` (`no_release_outside_range`), else null. An open set.

allOf.description: A fix of kind `unknown` or `none` has a `reason` and no `to_branch`; a known reachable kind has a branch and no reason; a kind this schema does not list is not constrained.
`on_installed_branch` and `newest` are null when there is no branch; `on_installed_branch` is set when there is one.
`php` is null for `unknown` and `none` (no fixing release known).

s9row.description: One counted advisory on the installed version. Ignored advisories are in `security.ignored[]`.

cve.description: Its CVE; null when it has none.

title.description: Its title without a leading `<cve>: `, so `{cve} {title}` never prints the CVE twice; trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed. Text, never markup: a page that styles backticks escapes them here.

link.description: Its advisory page; null when the repository serves none.

reported_at.description: When it was reported; null when the repository does not say.

severity_published.description: The raw word the repository published (`moderate`); null when unrated.

affected_versions.description: Its affected range as published; null when it has none (fix `unknown`, `affected_range_unknown`).

counted.description: True: S9 lists counted advisories only. Always true (an enum of one).

deciding.description: True on exactly the advisory the security term names.

s9.description: S9: the counted advisories on the installed version; fires exactly when an advisory counts (`select(.id=="S9")` means "has a counted advisory").

advisories.description: The counted advisories, deciding one included.

releases_read.description: Whether the releases were read and compared (report-1).

complete.description: Whether the advisory lookup for the package completed (`security.complete`).

s10.description: S10: a check the verdict rests on did not run; a confidence marker, never a flag. Unchanged from report-1 but for its known values.

unchecked.description: One entry per check that did not run.

signal.description: A signal: S1–S10 as in report-1, with the data keys report-2 adds; typed per id by the branches below.

summary.description: The signal sentence, `SignalSentence`: S1–S6 and S8 from their `data`, S7 from `data.packages[]`, S9 from `security` and the S9 rows, S10 from `data.unchecked[]`. Prose, not contract; key on the fields it is rendered from.

anyOf.description: A signal whose id this schema does not list, from a later release or not from lockrot: its data is any object.

activityEvent.description: What a forge's activity date measures: the last `push` (GitHub) or the last `commit` (GitLab, Bitbucket). An open set.

finding.description: One locked package judged: every key always written, nulls explicit; `spec_flags_r3.py` `KEYS['finding']`.

branch.description: The installed release branch; null for a snapshot. Equal to S8's `branch` when both are set, and to the installed branch row's.

installed_php.description: What the installed release itself needs from PHP: its own `require.php` from the lock entry (the branch rows' `php` is each branch's newest release's), and whether the target and the project admit it, as PhpFloor compares them. Not scored: a release the target does not run cannot be installed there unseen, Composer refuses it; every surface says it.

requires.description: The lock entry's php constraint as written; null when the entry declares none.

target_runs.description: Whether some version of the target PHP minor (`run.target_php`) satisfies it; null when `requires` is null or cannot be parsed.

project_allows.description: Whether the project's lowest PHP (`run.project_php_lowest`) satisfies it; null when either side is missing or cannot be parsed.

priority.description: `verdict` when graded, else `none`: a deprecated alias that leaves in report-3.

lead.description: The first counted maintenance flag; null when none counts. Equal to 0.13's verdict word on every 0.13-flagged finding: jq reads `.lead` where it read `.verdict`.

rank.description: Position in the run's order (`run.score_model.sort`), 1 first. A report writes `findings[]` in rank order, and re-sorting by `run.score_model.sort[]` gives the same order; an explain document carries the rank the package has in the run it explains. SARIF's `rank` is the opposite polarity.

flags.description: Every fired flag in flag order, accepted in place; each id once.

next_step.description: The move; null exactly at score 0.

checks_missing.description: S10 restated: the checks that did not run and raise S10.

checks_skipped.description: The checks that did not run and raise no S10: `repository_activity` (allowlisted, no repository, a path package, or the activity plan's cause for a registry-abandoned package), `release_metadata` (metadata that did not come, or a package not from a Composer repository), `advisories` (the composer-repositories scope, an installed version Composer cannot parse), `release_branch` (a branch snapshot: S8 cannot run). No `unchecked` gate reads it.

maintenance_judged.description: True exactly when `metadata.status` is `read`: repository metadata was read, so S2 and S8 ran. A finding can be graded with it false: a package not from a Composer repository is graded on the facts the lock holds (S1 marked in the lock, S5, S6), and its score-0 words (`without[]`, `if_counted`, `if_applied`) read `unknown`, never `ok`.

from_composer_repository.description: The lock entry carries a Composer notification-url (report-1): true exactly when `origin.kind` is `packagist` or `composer`.

origin.description: Where the lock entry came from (report-1's `packageOrigin`, unchanged).

replacement.description: 0.13's successor (report-1's key): S1's replacement when it is a package name other than the package itself, on a finding whose `abandoned` counts; equals `next_step.replacement.package` on every `replace` move, null elsewhere.

replacement_url.description: packagist.org's page for `replacement` (report-1); null when `replacement` is null or another registry named it.

note.description: The rendering of `metadata`; null when there is nothing to say. Prose, not contract; key on the fields it is rendered from.

libyears_unmeasured.description: Why `libyears` is null: the key of the report's `libyears.unmeasured` this finding is counted under. The reason is the first that applies, in this order: 1. not_from_composer_repository (no metadata was asked for: exactly the findings whose `from_composer_repository` is false, the lock entry carrying no Composer notification-url); 2. metadata_unavailable (asked for and did not come); 3. branch_snapshot (the installed version is a branch); 4. no_stable_release_date (no date lockrot trusts for one of the two ends; the code does not say which). The order of `x-known-values` is the block's key order, not this precedence. Null exactly where `libyears` is a number, 0 included. Counting findings by this value gives `libyears.unmeasured` key for key. An open set: a later minor release may add a reason, or split one into narrower ones, which moves findings out of the old code. Read a value you do not know as another reason the package was not measured.

direct.description: A direct requirement of the run.

dev.description: Listed under packages-dev in the lock.

reach.description: `unreached` = not direct, with an empty `chain`. Closed.

chain.description: From the direct requirement down to this package; one element when direct; empty when no direct requirement reaches it (report-1).

direct_dependents.description: The direct requirements that reach it (report-1); a transitive move names them.

signals.description: S1–S10 that fired, as report-1 orders them.

evidence.description: The join of the counted flags' `flags[].summary` (a flag counts when a `score.terms[].flag` names it) as `<id>: <summary>` in flag order; kept for jq. Empty exactly on the score-0 shape (no flag counts). Prose, not contract; key on the fields it is rendered from.

allowlist_reason.description: report-1's key, kept: the reason of an entry that accepts the whole package; null for a partial entry (`allowlist.flag_ids` set) and when no entry applies. Not an alias of `allowlist.reason`: read that for every entry.

data_date.description: The time of the newest repository data the finding read (report-1); null when lockrot read none.

libyears.description: Years between the installed release and the newest stable release, two decimals, at least 0; null when not measured (report-1, unchanged).

allOf.description: The verdict, its `priority` alias and the score's shape agree: a grade has the graded score; a score-0 word has the score-0 shape, priority `none` and no move.
`reach` follows `direct` and `chain`: `direct` when composer.json requires it; `transitive` with a chain of two or more; `unreached` with an empty one.
Maintenance is judged exactly when repository metadata was read.
`security.installed_branch_fixes` is null exactly when `branch` is (a snapshot).
`lead` is null exactly when no maintenance term counts; when set, the first term is the lead's own maintenance term.
An advisory counts (`security.status` vulnerable) exactly when the security part counts.
The `vulnerable` flag fires exactly when `security.status` is `vulnerable`.
The verdict is the band of `score.total` under score model 1: critical from 32, high 16 to 31, medium 8 to 15, low 1 to 7, a score-0 word at 0.
`dev` and a `dev` modifier go together on a graded score (modifiers are listed whenever their fact holds).
`reach` and the reach modifier go together on a graded score: none when direct, `transitive` when transitive, `unreached` when unreached.
`allowlist_reason` (report-1) is set only beside an entry that accepts the whole package (`allowlist.flag_ids` null).

A flag labelled `role: accepted` (a fired flag no term counts) stands only beside an allowlist entry; whether a flag counts is the join `flags[].id` ∈ `score.terms[].flag`, which this relation does not replace.
`gate.basis` is set exactly under a baseline entry (`baseline.recorded` an object).
A score-0 finding never stands `new` against a baseline: with no entry its `baseline` is null.
The security part's zero status follows the lookup: `clear` on a complete lookup, `unchecked` on a partial or unrun one; values this schema does not list are not constrained.
`security.move_in` points at a move that exists: `next_step` an object, `also` a non-empty `next_step.also`.
A package not from a Composer repository was never read (`metadata.status` `not_from_composer_repository`).

The score-0 word follows its condition (in precedence): `finished` when an allowlist entry applies (it accepts the whole package, or a partial `ignore[]` entry accepted a fired flag); else `unknown` when maintenance was not judged; else `ok`. A grade is not constrained here.
Under score model 1 each `without[]` row's verdict is the band of its total.
Under score model 1 each accepted flag's `if_counted.verdict` is the band of its total.
Under score model 1 each part's `alone.verdict` is the band of its total, null at 0.
Under score model 1 `next_step.if_applied.verdict` is the band of its total, a score-0 word at 0.
Under score model 1 each `next_step.also[].if_applied.verdict` is the band of its total, a score-0 word at 0.
Under score model 1 `security.partial.if_applied.verdict` is the band of its total, a score-0 word at 0.
Under score model 1 `gate.basis.verdict` is the band of `gate.basis.score`, null at 0.
Under score model 1 the band object follows the verdict: `floor` is the verdict's floor, and `to_next` is the next floor minus `total` (null at critical).
Under score model 1 each term of `gate.basis.new` carries model 1's weight for its flag or severity, and its divisor for its role.
Without a baseline standing no fact carries a baseline mark: `baseline` null makes every `flags[].baseline` and every S9 row's `baseline` null.
S9's level is `high` exactly when `security.worst` is `critical` or `high`.
A graded finding has evidence: the join of its counted flags' sentences is never empty.
An accepted flag fired: each `score.accepted[].flag` has its `flags[]` entry.
`metadata.reason` and `.message` are null when the metadata was read, and an `unavailable` status names its reason (MetadataFailure classifies every failure).
`evidence` is empty on the score-0 shape (no flag counts).
An entry that accepts the whole package (`allowlist.flag_ids` null) leaves no maintenance term and no lead.
A transitive or unreached package's `require` or `tag` move writes no `composer require` command (the package itself is never required at the root); its only commands are `composer why-not` checks.
Each `also[]` move of a transitive or unreached package's `require` or `tag` kind writes no command.
Without a counted advisory no move carries a fix kind: `next_step.fix_kind` and every `also[].fix_kind` are null.
`installed_php.requires` null (the lock entry declares no php) makes both of its answers null.
An accepted flag's `if_counted.at_least` is true only for `stale` (decided without S4).
Under score model 1 an accepted flag's `weight` is model 1's weight for it.
Under score model 1 an S9 row's `points` is its severity's points, doubled for the fix kinds that double (`none`, `blocked`); a fix kind this schema does not list is not constrained.
A snapshot whose release metadata was read carries the `release_branch` skip (`branch_snapshot`) in `checks_skipped`.
A degree's `liveness_complete` reads false only beside a `checks_skipped[]` or `checks_missing[]` entry that blocks S2 or S4.
A degree's `liveness_complete` reads true only when no `checks_skipped[]` or `checks_missing[]` entry blocks S2 or S4.
`from_composer_repository` is true exactly when `origin.kind` is `packagist` or `composer`; a kind this schema does not list is not constrained.

packageOrigin.description: Where a lock entry came from, as lockrot tells it from the entry and the manifest's own `repositories`, without asking any repository: `kind`, the `registry` where lockrot can name it, and the package's page there. Nothing in it is copied from the entry's URLs or the manifest's: a login, an organisation or a machine path is never written. Open: a later minor release may add a member.

package_url.description: The package's page on `registry`, an absolute https URL lockrot writes for a registry that keeps a public page per package name (`packagist.org`, `wp-packages.org`), from the name the lock records. Null for any other registry, for a name that is not a Composer package name, and for every kind but `packagist` and `composer`. It is the page the registry keeps for that name; whether this run's repositories still list the package is the finding's `note`. Show a link only when it is a string; read it, never build it, from `registry`, the name or anything else.

local.description: Whether Composer installed the package from the machine it ran on (a `path` or `artifact` repository, or a dist or source that is a path or `file://` URL) (report-1).

scoreRule.description: One rule of the model: in `stage` order, with its `kind`, its parameters (present by kind, below), a `why` id, a `doc` anchor and an engine-computed `illustration`. No prose: a page keeps its words keyed by id; an unknown id renders as `id` with the arithmetic its kind implies.

id.description: The rule id, without parameters. An open set: the ids model 1 uses are listed in `x-known-values`, and a later model may add one; an unknown id renders as `id`.

stage.description: Its place in the order of operations; stages are unique, 1–16 in model 1.

kind.description: What the rule does. An open set: an unknown kind renders the id and the finding's contribution only.

applies_to.description: What the rule acts on. Open.

why.description: Why the rule exists, an id the page words; an unknown `why` id is omitted. Open.

doc.description: The anchor of its doc section under `docs` (`score-divide-reach`).

illustration.description: An example lockrot computes with the same engine as every score, so a rule the report never exercises still shows its numbers; keys vary by rule (`before`, `after`, `band_before`, `band_after`, `severity`, `flag`, `total`, …); null when the rule has none.

order.description: The order a `select` or `cover` rule walks (`flag_order`). Open.

table.description: The model table a `lookup` or `zero` rule reads. Open.

when_fix.description: The fix kinds a `multiply` rule applies on (`none blocked`).

tie_break.description: The tie order of a `max` rule: points desc, severity in order, id asc.

collation.description: On an `asc` string key: `bytes` orders by UTF-8 bytes (PHP `strcmp`; in JavaScript compare code units, never `localeCompare`, which puts `_` before `-` and digits); null on every other key. Open.

when.description: The facts a `divide` rule applies on (`transitive unreached`, `dev`).

of.description: The rule an `exempt` rule exempts from.

op.description: The operation of a `combine` rule. Open.

ratio.description: The ratio of a `band` rule (each floor doubles).

ratio_from.description: The band from which the floors double (`medium`).

cap_multiplier.description: The cap of a `gate` rule (`min(score, 2 × new)`).

covers.description: What a `cover` rule covers (an entry covers each flag it lists and every flag below it). Open.

accept_group.description: On `counted`: the exclusive group within which an `ignore[]` entry's accepted flag also accepts the flags below it (`liveness`: abandoned covers silent and stale, silent covers stale), so a package that ages into the word the entry names never scores lower. Open.

accept_covers.description: On `counted`: what an `ignore[]` entry's flag accepts within `accept_group` (each listed flag and every one below it). Open.

anyOf.description: A rule kind this schema does not list: no parameter is required.

scoreModel.description: The score model, self-described: ordered flags, severities, fix kinds and bands, the rules with ids and illustrations, the sort keys with JSON paths. A "How the score works" panel is built from it alone. Any change to a number, a band floor, a rule's parameters, the doubling set, the sort keys or the gate or cover rule bumps `id`.

id.description: The model id (`score.model`, `score_model_id` in baseline-2): an integer; a document with no `score_model` (report-1) counts as model 0.

score_text_grammar.description: The version of the ScoreText grammar only. `run.text_grammar` versions the sentence grammars.

id.description: The part id (the vocabulary of `terms[].part`, closed).

flag_ids.description: Its flag ids, in flag order.

combine.description: How its terms combine. Open (the bump policy: every value a model change can add is open).

points.description: Its points; null for `vulnerable` (points come from `severities`).

band.description: The band its points reach alone (the pill tone); null for `vulnerable`.

can_corroborate.description: Whether it can follow another counted maintenance flag.

max_maintenance.description: The most corroboration can add under it as lead.

v013_base.description: The 0.13 band it is anchored to; null for `vulnerable`.

points.description: `band_floor` (its points are that band's floor) or `severities`. Open.

points_from.description: The table its points come from: `severities` on `vulnerable`; null on a maintenance row, whose `points` are its own (written on every row, as every report-2 key is). Open.

severities.description: The severity rows in the one order (critical, high, medium, unrated, low).

gate_rank.description: Its rank for `vulnerable-*` and re-rating (unrated has medium's rank).

counts_as.description: The severity it counts as (`unrated` → `medium`); null otherwise.

basis.description: How its points are formed: `{points: band_floor}`, `{points: counts_as}`, or `{points: share, of, share {num, den}}`.

of.description: On `share`: the severity it is a share of.

fix_kinds.description: The fix legend in ease order, with the `doubles` badge.

zero_verdicts.description: The conditions of the three score-0 words, in evaluation precedence (the first whose condition holds applies: an allowlisted package reads `finished` even without metadata); display order is `run.verdicts`.

exact_unit.description: The unit of `exact` and every contribution: 0.5.

max_total.description: The largest total the model can give (104), the bar's overflow cap.

bar_max.description: The bar's axis maximum (64; one block = 2 points).

bar_overflow.description: How a total above `bar_max` is drawn. Open.

holds_unless.description: When the group holds only under a threshold relation: it holds unless `threshold` is below `below` (`release_push`: stale beside left-behind needs push-warn-years below release-warn-years); null when it always holds.

sort.description: The default order of `findings[]`: each key with its JSON path, direction, default for an absent path and, for the verdict, the order itself.

path.description: Its JSON path in a finding (`score.parts.security.contribution`).

collation.description: On an `asc` string key (`package`): `bytes` orders by UTF-8 bytes (PHP `strcmp`; in JavaScript compare code units, never `localeCompare` or `Intl.Collator`, which put `_` before `-` and digits, so `foo/bar_x` and `foo/bar-x` would swap); null on every other key. Open.

default.description: The value when the path is absent (0 on the score-0 shape); null when the path is always present.

docs.description: The page that explains this model, versioned by model (`https://lockrot.dev/verdicts/model-1/`).

value.description: The value as parsed: trimmed, lower-cased (`high`, `left-behind`, `vulnerable-high`, `unchecked`).

kind.description: `grade` (0.13's `priority`), `flag` (0.13's `verdict`), `vulnerable`, `unchecked`. An open set, reason-like (underscores); no kind keeps the token `verdict`.

threshold.description: The grade, the flag or the minimum severity the value names (`vulnerable` → `low`, `vulnerable-high` → `high`); null exactly for `unchecked`.

not.description: `none` is the absence of a gate: `--fail-on=none` writes `gates: []`, never a `none` entry.

anyOf.description: A known kind but `unchecked` names its threshold.
A kind this schema does not list is not constrained.

allOf.description: A value's kind follows the value: the four grades are `grade`, the six maintenance flags `flag`, `vulnerable` and `vulnerable-<severity>` `vulnerable`, `unchecked` `unchecked`; a value or a kind this schema does not list is not constrained.

The threshold follows the value: a grade or a flag is its own threshold, `vulnerable` reads `low`, `vulnerable-<severity>` the severity, `unchecked` none; a value this schema does not list is not constrained.

run.description: What the run was told to do (`RUN_KEYS`): every key always written.

project.description: What the report calls the project: composer.json's `name`, or `extra.lockrot.project` (report-1); null where neither says.

root_package.description: The root package's own `name` (report-1); null where the manifest has none or no composer.json was read.

target_php.description: The target PHP minor (`8.4`) from the first link of the target chain that sets it, as MAJOR.MINOR (`8` reads `8.0`, `8.4.7` reads `8.4`), the form baseline-2 stores; always a string with `target_php_source` beside it.

target_php_source.description: Which link of the chain set it (`config` = `extra.lockrot.target-php`, `platform` = `config.platform.php`). Closed.

project_php.description: The project's `require.php` as written (report-1); never parse it.

project_php_lowest.description: The lowest PHP `require.php` admits: its lower bound normalised to MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, a fourth segment and a stability suffix dropped (`7.2.5.0-dev` is `7.2.5`, `^7.4.0-RC1` gives `7.4.0`; `7.2.0` for `^7.2 || ^8.0.0`; an exclusive `>7.4` gives `7.4.0`, a patch the project excludes in a minor it allows). Null exactly when the constraint has no lowest: no `require.php`, `*`, an alternative with no lower bound (`<8`), or a constraint it cannot parse. Print it with a trailing `.0` patch dropped.

lock_file.description: The name of the lock (report-1), never its path.

fail_on.description: The parsed values in kind order (grade, flag, vulnerable, unchecked; a list holds one value per kind), joined with `,`, no spaces, lower case (`high`, `left-behind,vulnerable-high`, `none`): one gate writes one string whatever order it was typed in. report-1's string type.

gates.description: The parsed list, at most one value per kind, in the kind order of `fail_on`; `[]` for `--fail-on=none`.

include_dev.description: Whether packages-dev were analysed (`--dev`): the graph then walks `require-dev` too, so a reach sentence names the requirements it walked. Equal to the report's root `include_dev`.

mode.description: What the run was asked to do: `check` or `generate_baseline` (report-1). An open set.

thresholds.description: The ages, in years, that separate one verdict from the next.

flag_ids.description: The seven flag ids in flag order (the vocabulary used, not a setting).

signal_ids.description: The ten check ids, for the Checks strip ("3 fired · 7 quiet").

fix_model.description: The fix classification's id; baselines compare fixes only under equal fix models.

text_grammar.description: The version of the sentence grammars: MoveText, GateText, FlagSentence, SignalSentence, NoteSentence, the suffix and the command renderings. ScoreText is versioned apart, by `score_model.score_text_grammar`.

score_rules_used.description: Rule id → the number of findings on which the rule changed or decided a number (each count's predicate is a field test: graded findings; score-0 findings for `zero-verdicts`; every finding with a non-empty `score.accepted[]` for `counted`), null only for `sort`. Keyed by `score_model.rules[].id`; an id absent from it shows no count. Keys follow the rule-id grammar, so a later id validates and a misspelt one (`corroborating_share`) does not; no property list, so it compiles as a TypeScript index signature. `x-known-keys` names model 1's ids, which a strict reader takes as the only keys.

^sort$.description: `sort` orders, it changes no number: always null.

^(([a-rt-z][a-z0-9]*|s([a-np-z0-9][a-z0-.description: A count: a rule id other than `sort`.

allOf.description: `fail_on` is `none` exactly when `gates` is empty (`--fail-on=none` is the absence of a gate).
`project_php_lowest` is null when `project_php` is (no `require.php`, so no lowest).
`verdicts` is the seven verdicts in their fixed order.
`graded_verdicts` is the four grades in their fixed order.

flag_ids.description: The seven flags, in flag order.

allOf.description: `flag_ids` is the seven flags in flag order.

signal_ids.description: S1 to S10 first, in order.

allOf.description: `signal_ids` begins with S1 to S10 in order (a later check is appended).
`none` stands alone in `fail_on`.

carrying.description: Graded findings with this flag counted.

leading.description: Findings whose `lead` is this flag: the number 0.13 counted under this verdict word (`counts.<flag>` in report-1), so a series read from report-1 continues.

accepted.description: The fired flags the allowlist accepts.

in_graded.description: On graded findings ("Accepted by the allowlist: none in flagged packages").

rootFlagVulnerable.description: `vulnerable`'s root counts: it has no lead and cannot be accepted.

carrying.description: Graded findings with a counted advisory.

leading.description: Always null: `vulnerable` is never a lead.

accepted.description: Always null: advisories are accepted in Composer's audit policy, never by the allowlist.

noteOffline.description: `offline`: the run was `--offline`, so repository metadata came from Composer's cache. No parameters.

noteMetadataUnavailable.description: `metadata_unavailable`: metadata was asked for and did not come for `package_count` packages. `reasons` groups them by message, in the order the text lists them, and their `package_count`s sum to the note's. Each such finding is `unknown`, with `libyears_unmeasured` `metadata_unavailable`.

package_count.description: Packages whose metadata did not come.

reasons.description: The failures grouped by message, in the order the text lists them.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteMonorepoParentUnavailable.description: `monorepo_parent_unavailable`: the monorepo whose tags date the packages split out of it could not be loaded, so their dates are their own. `parent` is the package a finding's `dated_by` would have named.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteAdvisoryIgnoreUnreadable.description: `advisory_ignore_unreadable`: Composer rejected the project's advisory ignore configuration, so every advisory counts. `message` is the first line of what Composer said.

message.description: Composer's own words about the project's `audit` or `policy` configuration, the first line, possibly empty; they quote that configuration, never a repository. Not contract.

noteAdvisoriesUnavailable.description: `advisories_unavailable`: one Composer repository did not return advisories, and the others were still asked. `composer_repository` is Composer's name for it, its URL cut as `message` cuts one; `message` the first line of the error, or its class when it has none.

composer_repository.description: Composer's name for the repository, its URL cut as `message` cuts one.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteAdvisoriesNotChecked.description: `advisories_not_checked` (0.13's code and data, reworded): no advisory was looked up, so no finding is graded for an advisory and each move's score after it assumes its versions carry none. One lookup per run asks every advisory of every name, so the installed versions and the moves' versions are checked together or not at all.

composer_repositories_checked.description: Advisory-capable repositories asked before the check stopped (report-1).

noteRepositoryActivityNotChecked.description: `repository_activity_not_checked`: no repository host was asked about activity; the findings it concerns carry S10 with the same `reason`.

noteRepositoryActivityAnonymousCap.description: `repository_activity_anonymous_cap`: without credentials for the host the run asked only about candidate packages, and at most a budget of them: `checked` were asked, `skipped_no_token` were not candidates (S10 `no_token` on their findings) and `skipped_budget` were candidates beyond the budget (S10 `anonymous_budget`). The text prints the two skipped counts as one sum. GitLab has no cap.

noteRepositoryActivityRateLimited.description: `repository_activity_rate_limited`: a host of this kind answered "too many requests". `repositories` lists every repository of this kind of host that got no answer, on each of its hosts, with its own message; the text's count is its length. Every package on this kind of host whose activity is missing carries S10 `rate_limit`, one whose repository answered 404 (listed under `repository_activity_not_found`) included.

repositories.description: Every repository of this kind of host that got no answer, with its message.

noteRepositoryActivityUnreachable.description: `repository_activity_unreachable`: the host did not answer for `repositories`, each with its own message; the text prints their count and the first one's message. Their findings carry S10 `fetch_failed`.

repositories.description: The repositories the host did not answer for.

noteRepositoryActivityNotFound.description: `repository_activity_not_found`: the host answered 404 for `repositories` (private, renamed or removed). An answer, not a network failure; where the host did not also rate-limit, this is the only record of them: their findings carry no S10 and their explanation's `activity` is null.

repositories.description: The repositories the host answered 404 for.

noteNotFromComposerRepository.description: `not_from_composer_repository`: `package_count` packages carry no Composer notification-url, so lockrot read no release metadata and no repository activity for them. Equal to the report's `not_from_composer_repository`.

package_count.description: Packages with no Composer notification-url; equal to the root `not_from_composer_repository`.

noteAdvisoriesDisabledByPolicy.description: `advisories_disabled_by_policy`: Composer's policy stops Composer blocking installs and updates on advisories. It only informs: lockrot still asks and counts every advisory.

policy_key.description: The full Composer config key, or the environment variable `COMPOSER_POLICY`. Open.

noteCode.description: What a run note is about. lockrot's codes are lower-case words; `<vendor>:<name>` is reserved for a note that does not come from lockrot, as it is for a signal id. A kind, not an identifier: a run writes one code once per forge, per Composer repository or per monorepo parent it concerns. A code keeps its meaning (a new meaning gets a new code) and is retired, never removed or reused. An open set: a later minor release can add a code; read one you do not know as another thing the run could not see.

noteDetail.description: One thing the run could not see or changed (report-1's typed notes): `code`, `data` typed per code, `text` the sentence every format prints. Every note's `text` is prose rendered from its `data` (NoteSentence).

text.description: Exactly the `notes` string at the same index: prose, not contract. Key on `code` and `data`, never on the wording.

docs_url.description: An absolute https URL on lockrot.dev for this code; null means no page, show no link; read it, never build it. Every URL lockrot has written keeps resolving for all of 1.x, though the page it opens may change.

sets_network_failures.description: Whether this note is part of why the root `network_failures` is true (report-1); false for every code report-2 adds.

data.description: The facts behind the note, typed per `code`; `{}` for a code that has none. Every key a listed code's data declares is always written.

anyOf.description: A note whose code this schema does not list, from a later release or not from lockrot: its data is any object.

path.description: The baseline file as a report names it: the configured path when it is relative, the path relative to the project directory when an absolute one is inside it, and the file name alone otherwise, so a report never locates the machine that wrote it.

stale.description: Baselined package names absent from the analysed lock.

baselineComparison.description: How the run compared with the baseline file (report-1, unchanged): the counts of findings by standing and the stale entries.

rootGate.description: The run's gate (report-1's) plus the finding counts the `gate:` line prints.

fails.description: The gate's decision. True: the run exits 1, unless it then fails to write a file or the baseline, in which case it exits 2 and says so on stderr. False: it exits 0, under the same proviso. True exactly when `tripped_by` is not empty.

tripped_by.description: What failed the run, each cause once: `strict_network`, `run.strict_network` is true and `network_failures` is true; `fail_on`, at least one finding's `gate.fails` is true. Both are listed when both hold. Empty exactly when `fails` is false. lockrot writes them in the order of `x-known-values`; do not rely on the position. An open set: a later minor release may add a cause; read a value you do not know as another condition that failed the run.

fail_on_applied.description: Whether the run judged its findings against `run.fail_on`: true in a `check` run, `fail_on` none included; false in a `generate_baseline` run, where only `--strict-network` can fail it. Where it is false no finding's `gate.fails` is true.

reaching.description: Findings whose `gate.reaches_fail_on` is true ("5 findings reach it").

exempt.description: Findings that reach and are exempt, by `exempt_by` value.

check.description: How the run's advisory lookup went (counted from the findings): the findings' one `security.check` value when they share it, `partial` when they differ, `complete` for a lock with no finding. An open set.

packages.description: Packages by `security.status`, plus those with an ignored advisory.

unchecked.description: Findings with `security.status` unchecked (never counted as clear).

severities.description: Counted advisories per severity, every severity present.

fixes.description: Vulnerable findings per `security.fix_kind`, every known fix kind present (fix kinds are open: a later kind is an extra key).

update_now_command.description: The one command the overview's "Update now" copies, as an argv list (`["composer", "update", <update_now…>]`); null exactly when `update_now` is empty, and then the line is hidden (a page never builds a command, and a bare `composer update` updates the whole lock).

oneOf.description: The argv: `composer`, `update`, then each package of `update_now` in its order.

fix_unknown.description: Vulnerable findings whose `security.fix_kind` is `unknown` (equal to `fixes.unknown`, kept for the CLI line).

allOf.description: `update_now_command` is null exactly when `update_now` is empty.
